description: Architecture guard of ddd-ts-kit: at session start, the next step of the plan, a one-line map per context and any gap between the version the skills describe and the installed packages; refuses hand-written generated files, a git command that skips the hooks of the project (read on the words of the command as the shell gives them), the writing of the baseline of the errors by an agent however the kit is launched, the code of a context in the main checkout of the trunk when the config requires worktrees and in a worktree of .worktrees/ without its own node_modules, writes of a context worker outside its bounded context, wherever the file stands (the checkout of the conductor, another worktree, outside every project but the temp directory) and from its first call, its shell commands that write outside that context or change dependencies, and any command but a read outside its own worktree, whatever the program and wherever its session stands (its git included: it lands nothing on the trunk, moves no other checkout, removes no worktree and writes no ref); reads the whole shell command (every command of it, a certain cd only, a name the shell computes, a wrapper, a package runner, and the writers the file tables miss) so a worker runs every command as cd <worktree> && ..., writes outside its worktree only to the devices and the temp directory outside every project, judges a file where it lands (a link followed, a file with another name refused), and is refused a command nested too deep to read, one with a quote or a here-document that never closes, one the reader breaks on, a dangerous git config (by an option, `--config-env` or a variable of the environment such as GIT_PAGER or GIT_CONFIG_*) and a Codex apply_patch the command does not hold (every patch of a line is judged as the editor tools are, a delete and a move held as rm is); pins its scope and the mode of the guard at its first call (a scope file removed or changed stops it until the conductor restores it, a config of its worktree that turns the guard off lifts nothing), notes before each command of a worker that runs code it cannot read (inline code, a script, a shell fed on its input, `make`, a test or package script: all but the pure readers, named by their name, git with no setting given to the command nor an option that hands the files to a program) the state outside its scope, compares it at its next call (a read keeps the note of the worktree, for what runs in the background) and at its stop (it goes on once to put a file back, and what stays reaches the conductor in its report and in status --workers), and stops it when that code changed a file there, deleted or committed included (a branch of its own merged back too: only what the trunk holds is the trunk's), until it is put back as the guard says (what the project's own format, lint:fix or regenerate script rewrites there being said, not held), a file left changed in the working tree of the checkout of the session (not one the conductor commits meanwhile) or a change of the packages the guard runs being said once for the conductor; refuses it another formatter; refuses the reviewer, the explorer and the verifier of the plugin any change of a file of a project by the shell; checks each written file, after the Biome of the project laid it out when the config says formatOnWrite; lets a sub-agent only remove pending(...) in an acceptance test, lets the acceptance-judge agent alone write a verdict on a locked acceptance (it reads git without adding or committing, and runs the kit only to read) and refuses its lock to any hand edit (a folder that holds the lock or the verdicts counts as them, git --output and rg --pre write); in the worktree of a story, refuses any change of its scope file (and of a worker's, in its worktree) to the session there and to every sub-agent, refuses the code of a context until each row has its design review and the acceptance is written and locked, says the phase of the story and where it meets the other open stories at session start, says once per file when a write meets another story, and refuses once to end before its report; in the worktree of a fix, opens the code once the regression spec is locked and refuses every edit of that spec, by the editor tools and by the shell, to its sub-agents (a folder that holds it counts as it, and so does a place only the shell knows, find -exec and xargs that write included); refuses to finish while architecture errors remain in a tree with uncommitted changes (a clean tree is left to the pre-commit hook and the pipeline; a check that does not end in time or answers more than the guard reads lets it finish and says so); reminds, without blocking, to commit a finished slice, and, in the worktree of a story, once when a done row departed from its design review without a compromise listed; warns a context-builder twice before its turn limit, records its runs in its worktree for `worker-scope --resume` and writes its final message as its report there (a sub-agent may not write the file), and at session start names the workers to resume. Reads only regular files, within a bound. Fails open, no network: a guide, not a security boundary (to isolate an agent, see docs/guides/agent-sandbox.md); it runs the project's own ddd-ts-kit CLI and Biome from node_modules (the bin each package names, never one installed above the top of the repository, and no config nor CLI in a folder another user may write, the shared temp dir above all), and of what code it cannot read writes, it compares only the git status and HEAD of the worktree and of the checkout of the session and the manifest and bin of the packages it runs: other ignored files (`node_modules`) and places outside those checkouts are not enumerated, and the state it keeps between two calls lies in the project, within reach of code that aims at the guard.
